title: Cyprus and Armenia Face Off in the Nations League
seoTitle: Cyprus vs Armenia in the Nations League
subtitle: Decisive October 2 match that could change the standings for both countries
excerpt: On October 2, the Armenian national team visits Nicosia to face Cyprus in the UEFA Nations League.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On the evening of October 2, Armenia plays the final round of Group 2 of League C of the UEFA Nations League against Cyprus in Nicosia. The clash decides who remains in the league and who risks dropping to the relegation play-off phase.

Table Standings and What Is at Stake

Before the matchup, Cyprus occupies second place in the group with four points, while Armenia is in third with three points. First-placed Montenegro has already secured the lead with nine points. The result of Cyprus vs. Armenia could determine whether the Armenian national team will avoid the relegation zone.

Lineups and Key Players

Cyprus took the field with Ribeiro de Freitas in goal and a midfield led by Kastanos, the team captain. In attack, Kakoullis and Loizou were the standouts. Armenia, managed by Eghishe Melikyan, had Beglaryan as goalkeeper and Hovhannisyan playing as a central midfielder. Striker Miranyan was the offensive focal point.

Broadcast and Kick-off Time

The match kicked off at 8:00 PM Yerevan time and was broadcast live on Armenian television channel H1, as well as being available on the OKKO TV platform. For international audiences, the match was accessible via streaming services covering the Nations League.

Recent Team Performance

In the competition, Cyprus had already recorded one win, one draw, and one loss, with four goals scored and two conceded. Armenia, on the other hand, won one match, lost another, and drew, scoring four goals and conceding five. Both teams have shown mixed results in their last six matches.

Standings Implications

If Cyprus wins, they consolidate second place and further reduce Armenia's chances of escaping relegation. An Armenia victory could elevate the team to second place, pulling them away from the danger zone. A draw would leave Cyprus with five points and Armenia with four, keeping the race tight until the final round.

With information from BBC, Sportaran.
